The House of Representatives created an investigatory committee to look into the judicial administrative processes of federal judges. In particular, the committee was tasked with investigating the issuance of court orders, the management of trial schedules, and the drafting of basic court documents by judicial assistants. The goal of the committee was to ensure that the administrative processes were carried out efficiently, accurately, and pursuant to federal legislation regarding the judicial administrative process.
After much investigation, the committee concluded that a federal district court judge was negligently mismanaging his trial schedule, causing undue delays in his case log. Based upon its findings, the committee made a recommendation to the House of Representatives to remove the federal judge.
Can the House of Representatives remove the federal judge based on the committee's recommendation?

A consumer sued a business in state court for allegedly violating a state consumer-protection law. The law contains an ambiguous provision regarding the requirements for consumers to bring deceptive-practice claims against businesses in the state. This provision in the state law is identical to one in a federal consumer-protection act and relies in part on definitions contained in the federal act. In its defense, the business claimed that, based on the ambiguous provision, it could not be sued under the state law. When the case reached the state's highest court, that court sided with the business, but it was unclear whether the court relied on the interpretation of definitions contained in the federal act. The consumer petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court for review of the state court's decision.
Is it constitutional for the Supreme Court to review the state court's decision?

A woman owns a luxury high-rise building in a large metropolitan area. The woman wanted to construct a helicopter pad on the roof of the building so that building residents could use a helicopter commuting service. A city inspector told the woman that she needed to apply for a permit to construct the helicopter pad, but he warned that the city would likely deny her application due to an existing zoning law. The woman promptly filed suit in federal court, seeking a declaratory judgment that the city's zoning law violates a federal law that prohibits state and local governments from restricting the provision of interstate transportation services to the public.
Which of the following is the city's best constitutional defense against this suit?

A political candidate wanted to run for office in an upcoming election and future elections. The candidate sought to be included on the state's ballot for the upcoming election, but she was unable to meet the requirements for certification.
The candidate filed suit in federal court against the proper representative of the state's electoral board, arguing that the state's requirements for ballot access are unduly burdensome and discriminatory. The district court ruled in favor of the electoral board, and the candidate timely filed an appeal. The election ended before the appellate court could hear the case. The state electoral board has moved to dismiss the candidate's appeal as moot.
How should the court rule on the state electoral board's motion?

A trade association in State A was formed for the purpose of protecting the state's lucrative cattle industry. The association's members, who are cattle breeders and dealers, use a grading system to grade the quality of cattle bred in the state. The grades assigned by the association are nationally recognized and prominently displayed on cattle to promote the state's cattle industry.
The commissioner of the agency that regulates cattle in State B has adopted a regulation that requires cattle sold in the state to display a grade approved by the federal government or no grade at all. The sales in State B of several members of the trade association have declined as a result of complying with this regulation. As a result, the association has filed suit against the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the regulation on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
May the court determine the merits of this suit?

Congress provides funds to states that can be used to reimburse medical providers for procedures they perform for low-income individuals. A state that participates in this federal program enacted a statute that prohibits reimbursing providers for the cost of performing vasectomies for men.
A doctor who routinely performs vasectomies for low-income men has submitted numerous requests for reimbursement pursuant to the program. However, the commissioner of the state agency administering the program has repeatedly denied the doctor's requests pursuant to the state statute.
The doctor sued the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the statute on the ground that it violates men's right to privacy.
Assuming that this federal district court has previously held that men have a privacy right to obtain vasectomies, how should the district court proceed with the doctor's suit?

An individual was physically removed from the premises of a privately owned shopping mall for passing out flyers in support of a candidate for mayor of the city in which the mall was located. The individual challenged this action in state court, contending that her removal violated the free speech provisions in both the U.S. and state constitutions. The trial court ruled in the individual's favor, and the mall properly appealed. The state supreme court concluded: "We hold that the state constitution, which protects free speech on privately owned property in certain situations, was clearly violated by the mall's conduct." The court declined to address the issue of whether that conduct violated the federal Constitution.
The United States Supreme Court granted a writ of certiorari to review this decision of the state supreme court.
How should the United States Supreme Court rule?

A federal statute, applicable to all public and private employers, makes discrimination against persons with a certain disability in the hiring or firing of employees illegal. It also provides for a civil action for damages against the offending employer. The statute contains a clear statement of Congressional intent to abrogate state immunity pursuant to its powers under the Fourteenth Amendment.
An employee sued her employer in federal court for violation of this statute and sought relief in the form of retroactive money damages. The employer, a state agency, moved to dismiss the action as constitutionally prohibited. The employee conceded that the state agency's acts, like most historical acts of discrimination against individuals with this particular disability, were rationally related to a legitimate government purpose.
Should the court dismiss the action on constitutional grounds?

Federal officials from the Environmental Protection Agency sought an injunction in federal court to prevent the owner of a hazardous waste facility from illegally discharging pollution from the facility into a river. Shortly before trial, the owner temporarily closed the facility for routine maintenance, which halted the discharge of pollutants into the river. The owner then filed a motion to dismiss the action as moot.
Should the court grant the owner's motion to dismiss?

A federal statute provides funds to private organizations that develop online learning materials for schools. A provision of the statute requires organizations that receive such funds to provide their educational materials to private, religious schools for use in their curriculum on the same terms that the organizations provide to public schools.
A taxpayer brought a suit in federal court to challenge the federal statutory provision as violating the establishment clause of the First Amendment. The taxpayer does not work in the education industry, nor does he have any children.
Does the taxpayer have standing to challenge the provision?

A state law that restricted access to contraception was challenged in state court as a violation of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution and as a violation of a similar due process provision of the state constitution. The case made its way to the state's highest court, which ruled that the law violated the due process provisions of both the U.S. and the state constitutions.
If petitioned to do so, may the U.S. Supreme Court exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision?

A wastewater treatment facility was fined for violating a state law regarding the discharge of pollutants into water sources. The facility challenged the fine in state court on the basis that the state law conflicted with federal law. In the state court's opinion, which sided with the facility, the court analyzed the state law in light of federal law regarding pollution and the water source where the pollutants were discharged but failed to clearly indicate the basis for its decision. On appeal, the decision was affirmed per curiam by the highest court of the state. The state appealed the decision to the U.S. Supreme Court.
Which of the following would be the most likely reason for the U.S. Supreme Court to review this case?

questions.question:
Under the authority of a federal voting rights statute, some states drew congressional districts in a manner calculated to increase the likelihood that members of historically disadvantaged minority racial groups would be elected. The U.S. Supreme Court declared these districts to be unconstitutional, as improper racial gerrymanders.
In response to this ruling, Congress passed a new statute that explicitly denies the Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction over all future cases challenging the constitutionality of action taken under the authority of the federal voting rights statute.
Which of the following is the most persuasive argument for the constitutionality of the new statute restricting the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction?

choices.a: Article III of the Constitution explicitly states that the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make.
choices.b: The constitutional principle of separation of powers authorizes Congress to pass statutes calculated to reduce the effects of Supreme Court decisions that interfere with the exercise of powers that have been delegated to the legislative branch.
choices.c: The establishment and apportionment of congressional districts directly affect interstate commerce, and the Constitution authorizes Congress to use its plenary authority over such commerce for any purpose it believes will promote the general welfare.
choices.d: The Fifteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to enforce the amendment's voting rights provisions by appropriate legislation, and Congress could reasonably determine that this restriction on the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is an appropriate means to that end.

Q82828 Under the authority of a federal voting rights statute, some states drew congressional districts in a manner calculated to increase the likelihood that members of historically disadvantaged minority racial groups would be elected. The U.S. Supreme Court declared these districts to be unconstitutional, as improper racial gerrymanders.

In response to this ruling, Congress passed a new statute that explicitly denies the Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction over all future cases challenging the constitutionality of action taken under the authority of the federal voting rights statute.

Which of the following is the most persuasive argument for the constitutionality of the new statute restricting the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction? 根据一部联邦投票权法规的授权，一些州以旨在增加历史上处于不利地位的少数族裔成员当选可能性的方式划分了国会选区。美国最高法院宣布这些选区违宪，认为其构成不当的种族不公正划分选区。

为回应此项裁决，国会通过了一项新法规，明确剥夺了最高法院对未来所有质疑依据联邦投票权法规所采取行动之合宪性的案件的上诉管辖权。

下列哪项是支持这项限制最高法院上诉管辖权的新法规合宪性的最有说服力的论点？
options:
A. Article III of the Constitution explicitly states that the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make.
《宪法》第三条明确规定，最高法院的上诉管辖权受制于国会制定的例外和规定。

B. The constitutional principle of separation of powers authorizes Congress to pass statutes calculated to reduce the effects of Supreme Court decisions that interfere with the exercise of powers that have been delegated to the legislative branch.
三权分立的宪法原则授权国会通过旨在削弱最高法院干涉立法部门行使授权权力的判决影响的法规。

C. The establishment and apportionment of congressional districts directly affect interstate commerce, and the Constitution authorizes Congress to use its plenary authority over such commerce for any purpose it believes will promote the general welfare.
国会选区的设立和分配直接影响州际贸易，而《宪法》授权国会为其认为能促进普遍福祉的任何目的，使用其对该贸易的全体权力。

D. The Fifteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to enforce the amendment's voting rights provisions by appropriate legislation, and Congress could reasonably determine that this restriction on the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is an appropriate means to that end.
《第十五修正案》授权国会通过适当立法来执行该修正案的投票权条款，国会可以合理地认定，对最高法院上诉管辖权的此项限制是实现该目标的适当手段。
data.explanation:
Article III exceptions clause


Congress can modify SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction unless modification would violate:
  • separation-of-powers doctrine (eg, by usurping judicial power) or
  • other constitutional provisions (eg, violating equal protection clause by only allowing men to appeal)


SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

Appellate jurisdiction is a court's authority to overturn, modify, or affirm another court's decision. The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has appellate jurisdiction over decisions by (1) lower federal courts and (2) the highest state courts when the decision turns on federal law. But Article III explicitly provides that this jurisdiction is subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make. Therefore, that is the most persuasive argument supporting the constitutionality of the statute restricting SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction.

(Choice B) The constitutional principle of separation of powers bars each federal government branch from usurping another branch's powers. And since a congressional statute calculated to reduce the effects of SCOTUS decisions may usurp judicial power, this argument does not support the statute's constitutionality.

(Choice C) The Article I commerce clause grants Congress plenary (ie, absolute) authority to regulate activities that, singly or in the aggregate, have a substantial impact on interstate commerce. But since establishing and apportioning congressional districts only has a mild impact on interstate commerce, this argument would fail.

(Choice D) The Fifteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to enact legislation to ensure that the federal and state governments do not deny or abridge the right to vote based on race, color, or previous servitude. But Article III specifically allows Congress to alter SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction, so it provides the more persuasive argument.

Educational objective:

Congress has the power to regulate and make exceptions to the U.S. Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction under Article III of the Constitution.

第三条例外条款


国会可以修改最高法院的上诉管辖权，除非修改会违反：
  • 三权分立原则（例如，通过篡夺司法权）或
  • 其他宪法条款（例如，通过只允许男性上诉来违反平等保护条款）


SCOTUS = 美国最高法院

上诉管辖权是法院推翻、修改或维持另一法院判决的权力。美国最高法院（SCOTUS）对（1）下级联邦法院和（2）当判决涉及联邦法律时各州最高法院的判决拥有上诉管辖权。但《宪法》第三条明确规定，此管辖权受制于国会制定的例外和规定。因此，这是支持限制最高法院上诉管辖权的法规合宪性的最有说服力的论点。

(选项B) 三权分立的宪法原则禁止联邦政府各分支机构篡夺另一分支机构的权力。由于一项旨在削弱最高法院判决影响的国会法规可能会篡夺司法权，因此这一论点不支持该法规的合宪性。

(选项C) 《宪法》第一条的商业条款授予国会全体（即绝对）权力，以规范单独或总体上对州际贸易有重大影响的活动。但由于设立和分配国会选区仅对州际贸易产生轻微影响，因此该论点不成立。

(选项D) 《第十五修正案》授权国会制定立法，以确保联邦和州政府不因种族、肤色或先前的奴役状况而拒绝或剥夺投票权。但是《宪法》第三条明确允许国会改变最高法院的上诉管辖权，因此它提供了更有说服力的论点。

教学目标：

根据《宪法》第三条，国会有权对美国最高法院的上诉管辖权进行规范并设定例外。

References

  • Ex parte McCardle, 74 U.S. 506, 514 (1869) (establishing that Congress has almost unlimited power to regulate and make exceptions to the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction).

data.htmlContent:
Constitutional Law

联邦法院管辖权解析

✅ 正确答案：A
最有说服力的论点是引用《宪法》第三条（Article III）的原文。该条款明确规定，最高法院的上诉管辖权（Appellate Jurisdiction）受制于国会制定的“例外和规定”（Exceptions and Regulations）。
⚖️ 核心法律原则：例外条款
本题考查的是国会对联邦法院管辖权的控制权，即所谓的Jurisdiction Stripping（剥夺管辖权）。
根据美国宪法第三条第二款，最高法院拥有两种管辖权：
  1. 初审管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)： 宪法直接赋予，国会不能通过立法剥夺或改变（参见 Marbury v. Madison）。
  2. 上诉管辖权 (Appellate Jurisdiction)： 宪法规定最高法院拥有此权，但“受制于国会制定的例外和规定”（with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make）。
因此，如果国会通过法律明确剥夺最高法院对某类案件的上诉管辖权，这在宪法文本上是有直接依据的。
📚 经典判例：Ex parte McCardle (1869) 在此案中，国会为了阻止最高法院审理关于《重建法案》合宪性的案件，废除了一项赋予最高法院人身保护令（Habeas Corpus）上诉管辖权的法规。最高法院裁定，根据宪法第三条的例外条款（Exceptions Clause），国会有权剥夺其上诉管辖权，因此法院驳回了该案。
❌ 为什么其他选项不佳？
选项 B 三权分立 (Separation of Powers)
这是一个陷阱。通常，“三权分立”是用来反对国会剥夺法院管辖权的理由（即指责国会干预司法独立）。虽然国会确实有权剥夺管辖权，但这权力来自《宪法》第三条的具体文本，而不是抽象的“三权分立”原则。
选项 C 商业条款 (Commerce Clause)
虽然商业条款赋予国会广泛权力，但划分国会选区（Gerrymandering）与“州际贸易”之间的联系过于微弱（Tenuous）。相比之下，选项A提供了直接的宪法文本依据。
选项 D 第十五修正案 (15th Amendment)
第十五修正案确实赋予国会执行投票权的权力，但这主要是实体法层面的权力。当涉及到法院管辖权这一程序性问题时，第三条（Article III）是更具体、更直接的权力来源。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到“国会限制最高法院管辖权”的题目时： 1. 检查是否涉及初审管辖权（如涉及大使、州为一方的案件）。如果是，国会无权限制。 2. 检查是否涉及上诉管辖权。如果是，国会有权根据“例外条款”进行限制（如本题）。
记住：直接引用宪法文本（Article III Exceptions Clause）通常是比引用一般原则（如三权分立）更强的论据。

questions.question:
City police officers shot and killed a woman's friend as he attempted to escape arrest for an armed robbery he had committed. The woman brought suit in federal district court against the city police department and the police officers involved, seeking only a judgment declaring unconstitutional the state statute under which the police acted. That newly enacted statute authorized the police to use deadly force when necessary to apprehend a person who has committed a felony. In her suit, the woman alleged that the police would not have killed her friend if the use of deadly force had not been authorized by the statute. The defendants filed a motion to dismiss the woman's suit.
How should the federal district court rule on this motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the suit raises a substantial federal question.
choices.b: Grant the motion, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits federal courts from deciding cases of this type.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the suit does not present a case or controversy.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the suit involves a nonjusticiable political question.

市警官在一名女子友人试图逃避其所犯持械抢劫罪的逮捕时，开枪将其击毙。该女子向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，控告市警察局及涉案警官，仅请求法院作出宣告性判决，认定警察行动所依据的州法规违宪。该新颁布的法规授权警察在为逮捕已犯重罪者所必要时，可使用致命武力。在该诉讼中，女子声称，若非该法规授权使用致命武力，警察本不会杀死其友人。被告方提交了驳回该女子诉讼的动议。

联邦地区法院应如何裁决此动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the suit raises a substantial federal question.
驳回该动议，因为该诉讼提出了一个重大的联邦问题。

B. Grant the motion, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits federal courts from deciding cases of this type.
批准该动议，因为第十一修正案禁止联邦法院审理此类案件。

C. Grant the motion, because the suit does not present a case or controversy.
批准该动议，因为该诉讼并未构成一个案件或争议。

D. Grant the motion, because the suit involves a nonjusticiable political question.
批准该动议，因为该诉讼涉及一个不可由司法审理的政治问题。
data.explanation:
Justiciability (suitability for judicial resolution)


Case or controversyProhibits advisory opinions under three doctrines:
  • Standing - plaintiff must allege injury-in-fact caused by challenged action & redressable by remedy sought
  • Ripeness - claim must present actual controversy involving past injury or present threat of injury
  • Mootness - claim must be unresolved
Adequate & independent state groundsSCOTUS cannot review final state court judgment that rests on adequate & independent state grounds
Political questionCourt cannot hear case if issue presented is reserved for executive/legislative branches or lacks judicially manageable standards for resolution
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

Article III restricts federal judicial power to actual cases or controversies - ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. As a result, federal courts can only issue a declaratory judgment if the dispute presents a real and immediate danger to a party's interests. Otherwise, the dispute would not satisfy Article III's case-or-controversy requirement since a judgment would amount to an impermissible advisory opinion - ie, a judicial opinion that determines the validity of a law without resolving an actual dispute.

Here, the woman sought a declaratory judgment that the state statute under which the police had killed her friend was unconstitutional. But the statute does not present a real and immediate danger to the woman since there is no indication that it poses any present or future harm to her. This means that the woman does not have any interest at stake to satisfy Article III's case-or-controversy requirement. Therefore, the federal court should grant the defendants' motion to dismiss the suit to avoid rendering an advisory opinion.

(Choice A) The woman's suit raises a federal question because she is challenging the constitutionality of a statute. However, the court must still dismiss her claim because no case or controversy exists.

(Choice B) The Eleventh Amendment bars private parties (and foreign governments) from suing states in federal court. But it does not apply to suits against local governments (eg, the city) or their affiliates (eg, the police department and its officers).

(Choice D) The political-question doctrine prevents federal courts from adjudicating issues that (1) are reserved to the executive or legislative branches or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution. But since federal courts regularly determine the constitutionality of state statutes, this doctrine does not apply here.

Educational objective: Article III's case-or-controversy requirement prohibits federal courts from issuing declaratory judgments unless the dispute presents a real and immediate danger to a party's interests. Otherwise, a judgment would amount to an impermissible advisory opinion.

选项正确率统计：A选项 17%，B选项 13%，C选项 58%（正确选项），D选项 10%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

可诉性（适合司法解决）


案件或争议 (Case or controversy)根据三项原则禁止咨询性意见：
  • 诉讼资格 (Standing) - 原告必须主张存在由被质疑行为造成的实际损害，且该损害可通过所寻求的救济得以弥补
  • 成熟性 (Ripeness) - 诉求必须呈现涉及过往损害或当前损害威胁的实际争议
  • 无争议性 (Mootness) - 诉求必须是未决的
充分且独立的州法律依据 (Adequate & independent state grounds)SCOTUS 不能审查基于充分且独立的州法律依据的州法院终审判决
政治问题 (Political question)如果所提出的问题是为行政/立法部门保留的或缺乏司法上可管理的解决标准，法院不能审理该案件
SCOTUS = 美国最高法院 (Supreme Court of the United States)

宪法第三条将联邦司法权限制在实际的案件或争议中——即可由司法解决的争端。因此，联邦法院只有在争议对一方当事人的利益构成真实且迫在眉睫的危险时，才能作出宣告性判决。否则，该争议将不满足宪法第三条的案件或争议要求，因为判决将构成一种不被允许的咨询性意见——即，在不解决实际争议的情况下，确定某项法律有效性的司法意见。

在本案中，该女子寻求宣告性判决，认定警察据以杀死其友人的州法规违宪。但该法规并未对该女子构成真实且迫在眉睫的危险，因为没有迹象表明该法规对她构成任何当前或未来的损害。这意味着该女子没有任何利害关系来满足宪法第三条的案件或争议要求。因此，联邦法院应批准被告方驳回诉讼的动议，以避免作出咨询性意见。

(选项A) 该女子的诉讼提出了一个联邦问题，因为她正在挑战一项法规的合宪性。然而，法院仍必须驳回她的诉求，因为不存在案件或争议。

(选项B) 第十一修正案禁止私人当事方（及外国政府）在联邦法院起诉州。但它不适用于针对地方政府（例如，市政府）或其附属机构（例如，警察局及其警官）的诉讼。

(选项D) 政治问题原则阻止联邦法院裁决那些（1）为行政或立法部门保留的或（2）缺乏司法上可管理的解决标准的问题。但由于联邦法院经常裁定州法规的合宪性，该原则在此不适用。

教学目标：宪法第三条的案件或争议要求禁止联邦法院作出宣告性判决，除非争议对一方当事人的利益构成真实且迫在眉睫的危险。否则，判决将构成一种不被允许的咨询性意见。

References

Ashcroft v. Mattis, 431 U.S. 171, 172 - 73 (1977) (holding that a father's emotional harm caused by the police shooting his son did not present an injury that would allow him to seek a declaratory judgment).

MBE 宪法考点解析

Judicial Review & Justiciability
正确答案：C

批准该动议，因为该诉讼并未构成一个案件或争议 (Case or Controversy)。

核心考点：可诉性 (Justiciability)

宪法第三条 (Article III) 限制联邦法院的司法权仅限于处理实际的“案件”或“争议” (Cases or Controversies)。

联邦法院禁止发布咨询性意见 (Advisory Opinions)。这意味着：

  • 法院不能仅仅为了解释法律而审理案件。
  • 原告必须证明存在具体的、实际的损害 (Injury-in-fact)。
  • 对于宣告性判决 (Declaratory Judgment)，争议必须对当事人的利益构成“真实且迫在眉睫的危险” (Real and immediate danger)。

本案逻辑推演

1
原告是谁？
一名女子，她是死者的朋友。
2
她想要什么？
她仅寻求一项宣告性判决，认定该州法规违宪。她没有索赔金钱损失（Damages）。
3
关键缺失：
虽然她的朋友已经死亡（过往伤害），但该法规对这名女子本人并没有构成“真实且迫在眉睫”的未来威胁。
4
结论：
既然该法规不会在未来伤害这名女子（除非假设她自己也要去犯重罪并逃跑，但这纯属推测），法院若判决该法规违宪，将无法解决她本人的任何实际争议。因此，这属于被禁止的咨询性意见。

判例依据

Ashcroft v. Mattis (1977)
本题改编自该真实判例。最高法院裁定：如果原告仅寻求宣告性判决，而该判决无法改变原告目前的权利状态或防止未来的伤害，则不存在“案件或争议”。

干扰项排除

选项 A (联邦问题)：
虽然案件确实涉及宪法（联邦问题），但这只是法院拥有管辖权的前提之一。如果原告没有诉讼资格 (Standing)，即使有联邦问题，法院也不能审理。
选项 B (第十一修正案)：
第十一修正案禁止起诉“州” (States)，但不禁止起诉“城市” (Cities) 或“地方警察局”。本案被告是市警察局，因此该修正案不适用。
选项 D (政治问题)：
审查法规是否违宪是法院的核心职能，不属于不可审理的政治问题 (Political Question)。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip) 当题目中原告寻求宣告性判决 (Declaratory Judgment) 时，请立即检查：
原告本人是否面临未来的、迫在眉睫的法律威胁？
如果是针对过去已经发生的伤害且不涉及赔偿，通常会因为缺乏“案件或争议”而被驳回。

questions.question:
A federal statute provides states with funds to establish a disability benefits program. The statute requires a participating state to disburse the benefits to eligible applicants within one month after an application is approved. A commissioner of a State A agency that established a disability benefits program pursuant to the federal statute issued a regulation that delayed the disbursement of benefits until six months after an application is approved.
Hundreds of residents of State A whose disability benefits were delayed because of the regulation have filed a class action against the commissioner in federal district court, arguing that the regulation violates the federal statute. The residents seek retroactive damages for the payment of the withheld benefits to be paid by the state treasury and an injunction to compel payment of future benefits. The commissioner has moved to dismiss the action and alleges that the requested relief is a violation of the Eleventh Amendment.
Should the federal court hear the merits of the residents' suit?

choices.a: No, because the commissioner is immune from suit under the Eleventh Amendment.
choices.b: Yes, but only on the request for retroactive damages for the withheld benefits.
choices.c: Yes, but only on the request for the injunction to compel payment of future benefits.
choices.d: Yes, on both because the suit is not subject to the Eleventh Amendment.

Should the federal court hear the merits of the residents' suit?

一项联邦法规为各州提供资金，用于建立残障福利计划。该法规要求参与的州在申请批准后的一个月内向合格申请人发放福利金。根据该联邦法规设立了残障福利计划的某州机构的一名专员，发布了一项行政规定，将福利金的发放推迟至申请批准后的六个月。

数百名因该规定而导致残障福利金被延迟发放的居民，已在联邦地区法院对该专员提起集体诉讼，主张该规定违反了联邦法规。居民们寻求追溯性损害赔偿，要求州财政支付被扣发的福利金，并请求发布禁令以强制支付未来的福利金。该专员已动议驳回此诉讼，并声称所请求的救济违反了 Eleventh Amendment。

联邦法院是否应审理该居民诉讼的实体问题？
options:
A. No, because the commissioner is immune from suit under the Eleventh Amendment.
不应，因为根据 Eleventh Amendment，该专员享有诉讼豁免。

B. Yes, but only on the request for retroactive damages for the withheld benefits.
应，但仅限于对被扣发福利金的追溯性损害赔偿请求。

C. Yes, but only on the request for the injunction to compel payment of future benefits.
应，但仅限于要求强制支付未来福利金的禁令请求。

D. Yes, on both the request for retroactive damages for the withheld benefits and the injunction to compel payment of future benefits.
应，对被扣发福利金的追溯性损害赔偿请求和强制支付未来福利金的禁令请求均应审理。
data.explanation:
Eleventh Amendment


(state immunity from suit in federal court)

Suit brought by private party or foreign government Suit against state official violating state law Exceptions:
ImmunityNo immunity
  • State consents to suit
  • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
  • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief
  • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
  • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. This immunity extends to suits against a state official for violating federal law when the state treasury, rather than the official, will be forced to pay damages that allegedly occurred before the action commenced (ie, retroactive damages). However, the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit suits against a state official when:
  • the official will pay the damages from his/her own pocket, which occurs when the official is sued for actions taken as an individual rather than as a government official or
  • the suit seeks a declaratory judgment or injunction , even if such relief would force the state treasury to pay money in the future to comply with the court order (ie, prospective damages).

Here, the residents filed a class action in federal court against the state commissioner, arguing that the regulation delaying their disability benefits violates the federal statute. The court may not hear the merits of their request for payment of the withheld benefits since such payments would constitute retroactive damages that would be paid by the state treasury (Choices B & D). However, the court may hear their request for an injunction to compel payment of future benefits because such payments would constitute prospective damages (Choice A).

Educational objective: The Eleventh Amendment bars suits against state officials for violating federal law when the state would pay retroactive damages. But it allows such suits when (1) the official will pay the damages or (2) the suit seeks declaratory or injunctive relief, even if the state would have to pay prospective damages under the court order.

选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 16%，C选项 37%（正确选项），D选项 38%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Eleventh Amendment


（州在联邦法院的诉讼豁免权）

由私人当事方或外国政府提起的诉讼；针对违反州法律的州官员的诉讼；例外情况：
享有豁免权不享有豁免权
  • 州同意被诉
  • 豁免权被第13、14或15修正案取消
  • 州官员因禁令性或宣告性救济而被起诉
  • 损害赔偿由州官员个人支付（而非州财政）
  • 州官员因将由州财政支付的预期性（非追溯性）损害赔偿而被起诉
  • 由美国或其他州提起的诉讼
  • 针对地方政府（例如，县、市）的诉讼
  • 破产程序
Eleventh Amendment 通常禁止私人当事方未经州政府同意在联邦法院起诉州政府。当州财政（而非官员本人）将被迫支付据称在诉讼开始前已发生的损害赔偿（即追溯性损害赔偿）时，这种豁免权延伸至因违反联邦法律而对州官员提起的诉讼。然而，在以下情况下，Eleventh Amendment 并不禁止对州官员提起诉讼：
  • 官员将自掏腰包支付损害赔偿，这种情况发生在该官员因其作为个人而非政府官员所采取的行为被起诉时，或者
  • 该诉讼寻求宣告性判决或禁令，即使此类救济会迫使州财政在未来为遵守法院命令而支付款项（即预期性损害赔偿）。

在本案中，居民们在联邦法院对州专员提起集体诉讼，主张推迟其残障福利金的规定违反了联邦法规。法院不得审理他们要求支付被扣发福利金的请求的实体问题，因为这类支付将构成由州财政支付的追溯性损害赔偿（选项 B 和 D）。然而，法院可以审理他们要求发布禁令以强制支付未来福利金的请求，因为这类支付将构成预期性损害赔偿（选项 A）。

教学目标： Eleventh Amendment 禁止在州政府需支付追溯性损害赔偿的情况下，因州官员违反联邦法律而对其提起诉讼。但它允许在以下情况下提起此类诉讼：（1）官员将个人支付损害赔偿，或（2）诉讼寻求宣告性或禁令性救济，即使根据法院命令，州政府将不得不支付预期性损害赔偿。

References

Ex parte Young, 209 U.S. 123, 159 - 60 (1908) (describing when the Eleventh Amendment does not bar suits in federal court against state officials for violations of federal law).

Edelman v. Jordan, 415 U.S. 651, 675 - 77 (1974) (holding that actions for injunctive relief against state officials in federal court are limited to those that result in the future payment of monetary damages from the state treasury).

32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 916 (2020) (explaining that the Eleventh Amendment bars citizens from suing state officials in federal court unless certain exceptions apply).

MBE 考点解析

第十一修正案与主权豁免

本题考察的核心是第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 下的州主权豁免权及其重要例外：针对州官员的诉讼。

核心原则：Ex parte Young (1908) 虽然第十一修正案通常禁止私人起诉州政府，但允许私人起诉州官员 (State Officials)，前提是：
  1. 针对的是官员违反联邦法律的行为；
  2. 寻求的是预期性禁令救济 (Prospective Injunctive Relief)。

关键区分：追溯性 vs. 预期性

根据最高法院判例 Edelman v. Jordan (1974)，联邦法院在处理此类案件时必须区分两种救济请求：

救济类型 是否允许？ 理由
追溯性损害赔偿
(Retroactive Damages) 		禁止 要求支付过去被扣留的福利金，实际上是从州国库 (State Treasury) 拿钱赔偿。这被视为直接起诉州政府，受第十一修正案豁免。
预期性禁令
(Prospective Injunction) 		允许 要求官员在未来遵守联邦法律。虽然这也会导致州政府花钱（支付未来的福利），但这被视为遵守法律的“附带后果” (Ancillary Effect)，是被允许的。

本题解析

题目中，居民提出了两项请求：

  1. 追溯性赔偿：要求支付过去被扣发的福利金。
    👉 结果：法院不能审理。因为这笔钱将直接来自州财政，属于第十一修正案禁止的范围。
  2. 未来禁令：要求强制支付未来的福利金。
    👉 结果：法院可以审理。这是为了制止官员目前和未来持续违反联邦法律的行为。

因此，正确答案是 C：法院只能审理关于未来福利金的禁令请求。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
看到起诉州官员 (State Official) 时，请立即检查“钱从哪里来”：
  • 如果是过去的损害，且钱从州国库出 ➡️ 禁止 (Barred)。
  • 如果是为了未来遵守法律，即使州政府要花钱 ➡️ 允许 (Allowed)。
  • 如果是官员个人掏腰包（个人责任）➡️ 允许 (Allowed)。

questions.question:
State A suffers from a high unemployment rate. To combat this problem, the State A legislature passed a statute requiring every business that sells over $5 million worth of goods each year in State A to annually buy goods produced in State A in an amount equal to half of its State A sales. Several persons and entities seek to challenge the constitutionality of this state statute in federal court.
Which of the following persons or entities most clearly has standing to do so?

choices.a: A company that sells $3 million worth of goods in State A annually but currently purchases only $1 million in State A goods.
choices.b: A distributor that currently does not sell or purchase goods in State A but expects to sell $15 million worth of goods in State A next fiscal year.
choices.c: A State B manufacturer that supplies 75 percent of the goods bought by a corporation with annual sales in State A of $10 million.
choices.d: The governor of State B on behalf of her state's businesses.

data.questionStem:
Q82189

State A suffers from a high unemployment rate. To combat this problem, the State A legislature passed a statute requiring every business that sells over $5 million worth of goods each year in State A to annually buy goods produced in State A in an amount equal to half of its State A sales. Several persons and entities seek to challenge the constitutionality of this state statute in federal court.

Which of the following persons or entities most clearly has standing to do so?

A州正遭受高失业率的困扰。为解决此问题，A州立法机关通过了一项法规，要求每年在A州销售额超过500万美元的每家企业，必须购买在A州生产的商品，其金额须达到其在A州销售额的一半。一些个人和实体试图在联邦法院就该州法规的合宪性提起诉讼。

以下哪个个人或实体最明确地具有诉讼资格？
options:
A. A company that sells $3 million worth of goods in State A annually but currently purchases only $1 million in State A goods.
一家每年在A州销售额为300万美元，但目前仅购买了100万美元A州商品的公司。

B. A distributor that currently does not sell or purchase goods in State A but expects to sell $15 million worth of goods in State A next fiscal year.
一家目前不在A州销售或购买商品，但预计下一财年在A州的销售额将达到1500万美元的分销商。

C. A State B manufacturer that supplies 75 percent of the goods bought by a corporation with annual sales in State A of $10 million.
一家B州的制造商，其为一家在A州年销售额达1000万美元的公司供应75%的商品。

D. The governor of State B on behalf of her state's businesses.
B州州长，代表其州内的企业。
data.explanation:
A federal court will not hear a case unless the plaintiff has standing - ie, a personal stake in the outcome of the case. This requires the plaintiff to allege three elements:

  • Injury-in-fact - actual or imminent harm that is concrete and particularized
  • Causation - the injury is fairly traceable to the defendant's challenged conduct
  • Redressability - a favorable judicial decision will likely remedy or prevent the injury


Here, the State A statute requires businesses selling over $5 million worth of goods each year in State A to buy State A produced goods in an amount equal to half of their State A sales. As a result, a corporation annually selling $10 million worth of goods in State A but purchasing 75% of its goods from a State B manufacturer must now buy more State A goods. This will cause the State B manufacturer imminent financial harm that can be prevented if the statute is found unconstitutional. Therefore, the State B manufacturer likely has standing to contest the statute.

(Choice A) The statute does not apply to the company that annually sells $3 million (not over $5 million) worth of goods in State A. Therefore, this company does not have standing to contest the statute.

(Choice B) The distributor that currently does not sell or purchase goods in State A but expects to sell $15 million worth of goods in State A next year will need to purchase $7.5 million worth of State A goods if its prediction is accurate. But it lacks standing to contest the statute because this harm is speculative - not concrete.

(Choice D) The third-party standing doctrine allows an injured party to assert a third party's rights in limited circumstances. But the State B governor does not have standing to sue on behalf of her state's businesses because there is no evidence that the statute injured the governor.

Educational objective: A plaintiff has standing to sue in federal court if he/she allegedly (1) suffered an injury-in-fact that (2) was caused by the defendant's challenged conduct and (3) is redressable by a favorable judicial decision.



选项正确率统计：A选项 15%，B选项 8%，C选项 71%（正确选项），D选项 4%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

除非原告具有诉讼资格（即在案件结果中拥有个人利害关系），否则联邦法院不会审理案件。这要求原告主张三个要素：

  • 事实上的损害 - 实际的或即将发生的损害，且该损害是具体和特定的
  • 因果关系 - 损害可合理追溯至被告的被诉行为
  • 可补救性 - 有利的司法判决可能会补救或阻止该损害


在本案中，A州的法规要求每年在A州销售额超过500万美元的企业，必须购买在A州生产的商品，其金额须达到其在A州销售额的一半。因此，一家每年在A州销售额为1000万美元但从B州制造商处采购75%商品的公司，现在必须购买更多的A州商品。这将对B州的制造商造成即将发生的财务损害，而如果该法规被裁定为违宪，这种损害就可以被阻止。所以，该B州制造商很可能具有挑战该法规的诉讼资格。

(选项A) 该法规不适用于每年在A州销售额为300万美元（未超过500万美元）的公司。因此，该公司不具有挑战该法规的诉讼资格。

(选项B) 一家目前不在A州销售或购买商品，但预计明年在A州销售额将达到1500万美元的分销商，如果其预测准确，将需要购买750万美元的A州商品。但它缺乏挑战该法规的诉讼资格，因为这种损害是推测性的，而非具体的。

(选项D) 第三方诉讼资格原则允许受损害的一方在有限的情况下主张第三方的权利。但B州州长不具有代表其州内企业提起诉讼的资格，因为没有证据表明该法规损害了州长本人。

教学目标： 如果原告主张其（1）遭受了事实上的损害，（2）该损害是由被告的被诉行为造成的，并且（3）该损害可通过有利的司法判决得到补救，则原告具有在联邦法院提起诉讼的资格。

References

  • Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560 - 61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).


  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 577 (2019) (explaining the injury-in-fact element of standing).

MBE 考点解析

宪法学：诉讼资格 (Standing)
⚖️ 核心规则：Article III Standing

联邦法院仅审理具有“诉讼资格”的案件。原告必须证明以下三要素：

  • 事实上的损害 (Injury-in-fact)：具体的、特定的、实际发生或迫在眉睫的损害。
  • 因果关系 (Causation)：损害可追溯至被告的行为。
  • 可补救性 (Redressability)：法院的有利判决可以解决该损害。
✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 C)
为什么 B 州制造商有诉讼资格？

案情分析：该制造商向一家在 A 州年销售额 1000 万美元的公司供应 75% 的商品。根据新法规，该客户公司必须购买 500 万美元（销售额的一半）的 A 州产品。

法律推理：
1. 经济损害 (Economic Injury)： 新法规迫使客户改变采购渠道，这将直接导致 B 州制造商的订单减少，造成具体的经济损失。
2. 因果关系： 这种损失直接源于 A 州的歧视性法规。
3. 可补救性： 如果法院宣布该法规违宪，市场将恢复自由竞争，制造商的订单有望恢复。

尽管法规直接监管的是 A 州的零售商，但 B 州供应商遭受了直接的经济后果，这足以构成 Standing。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A (年销售 300 万的公司)

错误原因：无损害 (No Injury)。
法规仅适用于销售额超过 500 万美元的企业。该公司未达到门槛，不受法规限制，因此没有遭受“事实上的损害”。

选项 B (预期销售 1500 万的分销商)

错误原因：损害具有推测性 (Speculative)。
最高法院在 Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife 中确立，损害必须是“实际的或迫在眉睫的”(actual or imminent)。仅有未来的意向或预测不足以构成 Standing。

选项 D (B 州州长)

错误原因：错误的诉讼主体。
通常情况下，州政府不能代表其境内的私人企业提起诉讼（即作为 Parens Patriae）。除非州本身拥有主权利益（如州界、州有资产受损），否则不能仅因其公民受损而起诉。

🎓 MBE 提分技巧 在涉及商业条款 (Commerce Clause) 或特权与豁免条款 (Privileges and Immunities) 的题目中，如果问谁有 Standing，通常寻找遭受直接金钱损失 (Direct Financial Loss) 的一方。

即使原告不是法规的直接监管对象（如本题中的供应商），只要法规导致其市场份额被挤占或订单流失，就满足 Injury-in-fact。

In the wake of massive terrorist attacks carried out inside the United States by foreign citizens, Congress declared war on the terrorists' nation of origin. It also passed a statute requiring every permanent resident who is a citizen of the enemy nation to either immediately leave the United States voluntarily or be subject to deportation. An inseverable provision of the new statute provides that the United States Supreme Court will have original and exclusive jurisdiction over any action brought to challenge the validity of the statute.
Is the new statute constitutional?

choices.a: No, because cases brought under the statute do not fall within the categories of cases specified in Article III as those over which the Supreme Court shall have original jurisdiction.
choices.b: No, because the statute violates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment.
choices.c: Yes, because among the powers of Congress enumerated in Article I, Section 8, is the power to enact laws governing immigration and naturalization.
choices.d: Yes, because Article III specifically provides that the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court shall be subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make.

data.questionStem:
Q82196

In the wake of massive terrorist attacks carried out inside the United States by foreign citizens, Congress declared war on the terrorists' nation of origin. It also passed a statute requiring every alien who is a citizen of the enemy nation to either immediately leave the United States voluntarily or be subject to deportation. An inseverable provision of the new statute provides that the United States Supreme Court will have original and exclusive jurisdiction over any action brought to challenge the validity of the statute.

Is the new statute constitutional?

在外国公民于美国境内发动大规模恐怖袭击之后，国会向恐怖分子来源国宣战。国会还通过了一项法规，要求每一位作为敌国公民的外国人要么立即自愿离开美国，要么将被驱逐出境。该新法规中一项不可分割的条款规定，美国最高法院对任何为挑战该法规有效性而提起的诉讼拥有初审和专属管辖权。

该新法规是否合宪？
options:
A. No, because cases brought under the statute do not fall within the categories of cases specified in Article III as those over which the Supreme Court shall have original jurisdiction.
不合宪，因为根据该法规提起的案件不属于Article III中规定的、最高法院拥有初审管辖权的案件类别。

B. No, because the statute violates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment.
不合宪，因为该法规违反了第五修正案的平等保护条款。

C. Yes, because among the powers of Congress enumerated in Article I, Section 8, is the power to enact laws governing immigration and naturalization.
合宪，因为在Article I, Section 8中列举的国会权力中，包括制定有关移民和归化法律的权力。

D. Yes, because Article III specifically provides that the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court shall be subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make.
合宪，因为Article III明确规定，最高法院的管辖权应受国会制定的例外和规章的约束。

SCOTUS jurisdiction


TypeDefinitionApplicability
OriginalCase filed directly in SCOTUS

(Congress cannot adjust)		Cases involving either:
ambassador/public minister/consul or
state as party
AppellateCase filed after decision by either:
lower federal court or
highest state court

(Congress may limit)		All other cases by either:
writ of certiorari or
direct appeal (rare)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

Original jurisdiction is a court's power to hear and decide a case first - ie, before any appellate review. Article III provides that the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has original jurisdiction over:
  • cases involving foreign ambassadors, public ministers, or consuls and
  • cases in which a state is a party.
And though Congress has the power to limit SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction, Congress cannot alter SCOTUS's original jurisdiction (Choice D).

Here, Congress passed a statute requiring every alien who is a citizen of the enemy nation to leave the United States voluntarily or be subject to deportation. The statute provides that SCOTUS will have original and exclusive jurisdiction over any action challenging the statute's validity. Since this inseverable provision purports to expand SCOTUS's original jurisdiction beyond the categories of cases specified in Article III, the statute is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) Federal classifications based on alienage are subject to mere rational basis scrutiny under the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment. That is because Congress has plenary (ie, exclusive) authority to make immigration policy. And since the deportation order is rationally related to the government's legitimate interest in national security, the statute does not violate this component.

(Choice C) Article I, Section 8 enumerates Congress's powers, including the power to enact laws governing immigration and naturalization. But Congress cannot violate other constitutional provisions when exercising these powers (as seen here).

Educational objective: The United States Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over (1) cases in which a state is a party and (2) cases involving foreign ambassadors, public ministers, or consuls. Congress cannot expand or limit this jurisdiction.

选项正确率统计：A选项 54%（正确选项），B选项 20%，C选项 15%，D选项 10%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

SCOTUS 管辖权


类型定义适用性
初审直接向SCOTUS提起的案件

(国会不能调整)		涉及以下任一情况的案件：
大使/公使/领事 或
州为一方当事人
上诉在以下任一法院作出判决后提起的案件：
下级联邦法院 或
州最高法院

(国会可以限制)		所有其他案件通过以下任一方式：
调卷令 或
直接上诉（罕见）
SCOTUS = 美国最高法院

初审管辖权是法院在任何上诉复审之前，首次审理和裁决案件的权力。Article III规定，美国最高法院（SCOTUS）对以下案件拥有初审管辖权：
  • 涉及外国大使、公使或领事的案件，以及
  • 州为一方当事人的案件。
尽管国会有权限制SCOTUS的上诉管辖权，但国会不能改变SCOTUS的初审管辖权（选项 D）。

在本案中，国会通过了一项法规，要求每一位作为敌国公民的外国人自愿离开美国，否则将被驱逐出境。该法规规定，SCOTUS对任何挑战该法规有效性的诉讼拥有初审和专属管辖权。由于这项不可分割的条款意图将SCOTUS的初审管辖权扩展到Article III规定的案件类别之外，因此该法规是违宪的。

（选项 B）基于国籍的联邦分类，根据第五修正案的平等保护条款，仅需接受合理基础审查。这是因为国会在制定移民政策方面拥有全体（即专属）权力。并且，由于驱逐令与政府在国家安全方面的合法利益有合理关联，该法规并未违反此条款。

（选项 C）Article I, Section 8列举了国会的权力，包括制定有关移民和归化的法律的权力。但国会在行使这些权力时，不能违反宪法的其他规定（如此处所示）。

教学目标：美国最高法院对以下案件拥有初审管辖权：（1）州为一方当事人的案件，以及（2）涉及外国大使、公使或领事的案件。国会不能扩大或限制此管辖权。

References

Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. 137, 174 - 76 (1803) (holding that Congress cannot expand the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction).

32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 453 (2019) (defining original and appellate jurisdiction).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review
核心考点：最高法院的管辖权 本题考查的是美国宪法第三条（Article III）关于最高法院（SCOTUS）初审管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction) 的限制。
法律规则解析

根据美国宪法第三条，最高法院的管辖权分为两类：

类型 范围 (Scope) 国会的权力
初审管辖权
(Original Jurisdiction)		 1. 涉及大使、公使、领事的案件
2. 州作为一方当事人的案件		 不能扩大或缩小
(Self-executing)
上诉管辖权
(Appellate Jurisdiction)		 所有其他联邦案件 可以限制/监管
(Exceptions Clause)

关键判例： Marbury v. Madison (1803)。在该案中，Marshall 大法官确立了一个原则：国会不能通过立法扩大宪法第三条规定的最高法院的初审管辖权。

案情分析

事实：国会通过了一项法规，规定最高法院对挑战该法规的诉讼拥有“初审和专属管辖权”（Original and exclusive jurisdiction）。

推理：

  • 挑战驱逐出境法规的案件，既不涉及外交使节，也不是州作为一方当事人的案件。
  • 因此，这些案件不属于宪法第三条列举的初审管辖权范围。
  • 国会试图通过普通立法（Statute）将此类案件塞进最高法院的初审管辖权中，这违反了宪法。

结论：该法规违宪。正确答案是 A。

干扰项排除技巧

❌ 选项 D (Exceptions Clause Trap)：

这是最强的干扰项。宪法确实规定最高法院的管辖权受制于国会的“例外和规章”（Exceptions and Regulations）。但请注意：这仅适用于上诉管辖权 (Appellate Jurisdiction)，不适用于初审管辖权。

❌ 选项 B (Equal Protection)：

虽然涉及基于国籍的分类，但在移民和国家安全领域，国会拥有绝对权力 (Plenary Power)。针对敌国公民的驱逐通常能通过合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)，因此不太可能违反平等保护条款。

❌ 选项 C (Immigration Power)：

国会确实有权制定移民法（Article I, Section 8）。但是，国会不能使用其立法权来违反宪法的结构性条款（如Article III对法院管辖权的限制）。权力必须在宪法框架内行使。

考试贴士： 看到 "Congress expands SCOTUS original jurisdiction"（国会扩大最高法院初审管辖权）时，直接选违宪。这是 Marbury v. Madison 的核心教义。

questions.question:
A plaintiff challenged the constitutionality of a state tax law, alleging that it violated the equal protection clauses of both the United States Constitution and the state constitution. The state supreme court agreed and held the tax law to be invalid. It said: "We hold that this state tax law violates the equal protection clause of the United States Constitution and also the equal protection clause of the state constitution because we interpret that provision of the state constitution to contain exactly the same prohibition against discriminatory legislation as is contained in the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution."
The state sought review of this decision in the United States Supreme Court, alleging that the state supreme court's determination of the federal constitutional issue was incorrect.
How should the United States Supreme Court dispose of the case if it believes that this interpretation of the federal Constitution by the state supreme court raises an important federal question and is incorrect on the merits?

choices.a: Refuse to review the decision of the state supreme court, because a state government may not seek review of decisions of its own courts in the United States Supreme Court.
choices.b: Refuse to review the decision of the state supreme court, because it is based on an adequate and independent ground of state law.
choices.c: Reverse the state supreme court decision, because the equal protection clause of a state constitution must be construed by the state supreme court in a manner that is congruent with the meaning of the equal protection clause of the federal Constitution.
choices.d: Reverse the state supreme court decision with respect to the equal protection clause of the federal Constitution and remand the case to the state supreme court for further proceedings, because the state and federal constitutional issues are so intertwined that the federal issue must be decided so that this case may be disposed of properly.

The state supreme court agreed and held the tax law to be invalid. The state sought review of this decision in the United States Supreme Court, alleging that the state supreme court's determination of the federal constitutional issue was incorrect.

How should the United States Supreme Court dispose of the case if it believes that this interpretation of the federal Constitution by the state supreme court raises an important federal question and is incorrect on the merits?

一名原告对某州税法的合宪性提出质疑，声称其违反了 United States Constitution 和州宪法的平等保护条款。州最高法院同意并裁定该税法无效。法院称：“我们裁定，该州税法违反了 United States Constitution 的平等保护条款，也违反了州宪法的平等保护条款，因为我们对州宪法该条款的解释是，其包含了与 United States Constitution 第十四修正案（Fourteenth Amendment）的平等保护条款完全相同的、禁止歧视性立法的规定。”

该州请求 United States Supreme Court 复审此判决，声称州最高法院对联邦宪法问题的裁决不正确。

如果 United States Supreme Court 认为州最高法院对联邦宪法的此项解释提出了一个重要的联邦问题，并且在实体问题上是不正确的，那么它应该如何处置此案？
options:
A. Refuse to review the decision of the state supreme court, because a state government may not seek review of decisions of its own courts in the United States Supreme Court.
拒绝复审州最高法院的判决，因为州政府不得请求 United States Supreme Court 复审其本州法院的判决。

B. Refuse to review the decision of the state supreme court, because it is based on an adequate and independent ground of state law.
拒绝复审州最高法院的判决，因为该判决基于充分且独立的州法律依据。

C. Reverse the state supreme court decision, because the equal protection clause of a state constitution must be construed by the state supreme court in a manner that is congruent with the meaning of the equal protection clause of the federal Constitution.
推翻州最高法院的判决，因为州宪法的平等保护条款必须由州最高法院以与联邦宪法平等保护条款含义相一致的方式进行解释。

D. Reverse the state supreme court decision with respect to the equal protection clause of the federal Constitution and remand the case to the state supreme court for further proceedings, because the state and federal constitutional issues are so intertwined that the federal issue must be decided so that this case may be disposed of properly.
就联邦宪法的平等保护条款推翻州最高法院的判决，并将案件发回州最高法院进行进一步审理，因为州宪法问题与联邦宪法问题紧密交织，必须对联邦问题作出裁定，此案才能得到妥善处理。
data.explanation:
The Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) has appellate jurisdiction over most final state-court decisions that present a federal question. But SCOTUS cannot exercise jurisdiction over, or review the merits of, such decisions if they are based on adequate and independent state grounds. This occurs when:
  • state law fully resolves the issue and the outcome of the case is not affected by federal law (ie, adequate state grounds) and
  • the final state-court decision is reached without relying on federal precedent (ie, independent state grounds).
Here, the state supreme court held that the state tax law violates the equal protection clauses of both the federal and state constitutions (adequate state grounds). But since that decision relied on the federal constitution to interpret the state constitution (no independent state grounds), SCOTUS has jurisdiction to reverse † the state's interpretation of the federal constitution (Choice B). Once it does so (resolving the federal question), it must then remand the case to the state supreme court for further proceedings on the remaining state-law issues.

†A remand would be unnecessary if SCOTUS agreed with (ie, affirmed) the state's interpretation of the federal constitution since there would be no issues remaining to be settled.

(Choice A) A state government can seek SCOTUS review of its own state-court decisions so long as they are not based on adequate and independent state grounds (as seen here).

(Choice C) States are not required to construe their constitutions in a manner congruent (ie, consistent) with the U.S. Constitution because states can always grant broader constitutional protections.

Educational objective: SCOTUS has discretion to exercise appellate jurisdiction over state supreme court decisions that present a federal question - unless those decisions are based on adequate and independent state grounds. But once it resolves the federal question, SCOTUS must remand the case to the state supreme court if any state-law issues remain.



选项正确率统计：A选项 3%，B选项 31%，C选项 12%，D选项 52%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

美国最高法院（Supreme Court of the United States, SCOTUS）对大多数涉及联邦问题的州法院终审判决拥有上诉管辖权。但如果这些判决是基于充分且独立的州法律依据，SCOTUS 不能对其行使管辖权或复审其实体问题。这种情况发生在：
  • 州法律完全解决了争议问题，且案件结果不受联邦法律影响（即，充分的州法律依据）并且
  • 州法院的最终判决是在未依赖联邦判例的情况下作出的（即，独立的州法律依据）。
在本案中，州最高法院裁定州税法违反了联邦和州宪法的平等保护条款（构成充分的州法律依据）。但由于该判决依赖联邦宪法来解释州宪法（不构成独立的州法律依据），SCOTUS 有管辖权推翻†州法院对联邦宪法的解释（选项 B）。一旦这么做（解决了联邦问题），就必须将案件发回州最高法院，就剩余的州法律问题进行进一步审理。

†如果 SCOTUS 同意（即维持）州法院对联邦宪法的解释，则无需发回重审，因为将没有剩余问题需要解决。

(选项A) 只要其本州法院的判决不是基于充分且独立的州法律依据（如本案所示），州政府可以请求 SCOTUS 对其进行复审。

(选项C) 各州不被要求以与 U.S. Constitution 相一致（即，congruent）的方式解释其州宪法，因为各州总是可以授予更广泛的宪法保护。

教学目标：SCOTUS 对涉及联邦问题的州最高法院判决有行使上诉管辖权的自由裁量权——除非这些判决基于充分且独立的州法律依据。但是，一旦解决了联邦问题，如果仍有任何州法律问题待决，SCOTUS 必须将案件发回州最高法院。

References

4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 46 (2019) (explaining that state and federal grounds are interwoven when the state court decides that the state provision is identical to the federal provision).

MBE 考点解析

Judicial Review & State Grounds
核心原则：充分且独立的州法依据
Adequate and Independent State Grounds (AISG)
案情关键点分析

本案中，州最高法院虽然依据州宪法判决税法无效，但其判决书中明确指出：

“我们对州宪法的解释...包含了与联邦宪法完全相同的禁令。”

这意味着州法院对州法的解释并非独立（Not Independent），而是完全依赖于对联邦宪法的理解。

法律推理逻辑
  • 一般规则：如果州法院的判决基于“充分且独立的州法依据”，美国最高法院（SCOTUS）通常不会复审，因为即使推翻了联邦法部分的裁决，案件结果（基于州法）也不会改变，这会使 SCOTUS 的意见成为无实质效力的“咨询意见”（Advisory Opinion）。
  • 本案例外 (Michigan v. Long)：当州法院判决看起来涉及联邦问题，且没有明确声明其判决仅基于州法依据时，SCOTUS 会假定该判决受联邦法影响。
  • 紧密交织 (Intertwined)：本案中，州法院明确表示其州法解释与联邦法“完全相同”。因此，如果州法院对联邦法的理解是错误的，那么其对州法的理解也是基于这个错误的。
✅ 正确答案：选项 D

推翻并重审 (Reverse and Remand)

SCOTUS 应当推翻州法院关于联邦宪法的错误解释，并将案件发回（Remand）。

理由：既然州法院将州法与联邦法捆绑在一起，SCOTUS 需要纠正联邦法层面的错误。纠正后，州法院有机会在正确的联邦法标准下重新审视案件，或者明确表示即使联邦法允许，州法依然禁止该行为（行使独立的州主权）。

易错陷阱：选项 B

很多考生看到“州宪法”就选 B（拒绝复审）。
错误原因：这里的州法依据不独立（Not Independent）。只有当州法院说“无论联邦宪法如何规定，我们的州宪法都独立地禁止此行为”时，才是 AISG。本案中，州法院说的是“我们照搬联邦宪法的含义”。

其他选项排除
  • 选项 A：错误。州政府完全有权请求 SCOTUS 复审其本州法院的判决，只要涉及联邦问题。
  • 选项 C：错误。各州不需要（Not required）将其宪法解释得与联邦宪法一致。各州可以给予公民比联邦宪法更多的保护（但不能更少）。
MBE Constitutional Law Review
Focus: Jurisdiction & AISG

questions.question:
A woman contracted for expensive cable television service for a period of six months solely to view the televised trial of a man who was on trial for murder in a state court. In the midst of the trial, the judge prohibited any further televising of the man's trial because the judge concluded that the presence of television cameras was disruptive.
The woman brought an action in a federal district court against the judge in the man's case and sought an injunction that would require the judge to resume the televising of the man's trial. The woman alleged that the judge's order to stop televising the trial deprived her of property—her investment in cable television service—without due process of law.
Before the woman's case came to trial, the man's criminal trial concluded in a conviction and sentencing. There do not appear to be any obvious errors in the proceeding that led to the result in the man's case. After the man's conviction and sentencing, the judge moved to dismiss the woman's suit.
What is the most proper disposition of this motion by the federal court?

choices.a: Defer action on the motion until after any appellate proceedings in the man's case have concluded, because the man might appeal, his conviction might be set aside, he might be tried again, and television cameras might be barred from the new trial.
choices.b: Defer action on the motion until after the state's supreme court expresses a view on its proper disposition, because the state law of mootness governs suits in federal court when the federal case is inexorably intertwined with a state proceeding.
choices.c: Deny the motion, because the woman has raised an important constitutional question—whether her investment in cable service solely to view the man's trial is protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the subject matter of the controversy between the woman and the judge has ceased to exist and there is no strong likelihood that it will be revived.

一名女子签订了一份为期六个月的昂贵有线电视服务合同，其唯一目的是观看一名男子在州法院因谋杀罪受审的电视直播。在审判过程中，法官禁止对该男子的审判进行任何进一步的电视转播，因为法官认定电视摄像机的存在具有干扰性。

该女子向联邦地区法院对审理该男子案件的法官提起诉讼，并寻求一项禁令，要求法官恢复对该男子审判的电视直播。该女子声称，法官停止电视直播审判的命令，未经正当法律程序剥夺了她的财产——即她为有线电视服务所作的投资。

在该女子的案件开庭审理之前，该男子的刑事审判已经以定罪和判刑告终。导致该男子案件结果的程序中，似乎没有任何明显错误。在该男子被定罪和判刑后，法官提出动议，要求驳回该女子的诉讼。

联邦法院对此动议最适当的处置是什么？
options:
A. Defer action on the motion until after any appellate proceedings in the man's case have concluded, because the man might appeal, his conviction might be set aside, he might be tried again, and television cameras might be barred from the new trial.
推迟对动议的处理，直至该男子案件的任何上诉程序结束后，因为该男子可能会上诉，其定罪可能被撤销，他可能被重审，而新的审判可能会禁止电视摄像机进入。

B. Defer action on the motion until after the state's supreme court expresses a view on its proper disposition, because the state law of mootness governs suits in federal court when the federal case is inexorably intertwined with a state proceeding.
推迟对动议的处理，直至州最高法院就其适当处置发表意见后，因为当联邦案件与州程序密不可分地交织在一起时，州的已失时效法管辖联邦法院的诉讼。

C. Deny the motion, because the woman has raised an important constitutional question - whether her investment in cable service solely to view the man's trial is protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.
驳回该动议，因为该女子提出了一个重要的宪法问题——即她仅为观看该男子审判而对有线电视服务进行的投资，是否受到《Fourteenth Amendment》正当法律程序条款的保护。

D. Grant the motion, because the subject matter of the controversy between the woman and the judge has ceased to exist and there is no strong likelihood that it will be revived.
批准该动议，因为该女子与法官之间的争议标的已不复存在，并且不大可能重新出现。
data.explanation:
Federal courts have the power to decide actual cases and controversies - ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. But once the plaintiff's harm is resolved, his/her claim becomes moot and should be dismissed unless:

the harm is capable of repetition yet evading review due to a reasonable chance that the same harm will (1) affect the plaintiff again and (2) not last long enough to be fully litigated (eg, pregnancy) or the defendant voluntarily stops the challenged action but can resume it at any time.

Here, the woman sued in federal court to force the judge to resume televising the man's murder trial. But before the court could consider her claim, this controversy ceased to exist because the man was convicted and sentenced. And the controversy is not likely to be revived since there were no obvious errors in the man's trial warranting a new trial. Therefore, this controversy is moot, and the federal court should grant the judge's motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) It is highly unlikely that the man will succeed on appeal. But even if he does and obtains a new trial, it is pure speculation whether television cameras will again be barred from the courtroom. Therefore, the woman's suit is moot and should be dismissed - not deferred.

(Choice B) Federal courts always apply federal law to decide procedural issues like mootness - even when the federal case is inexorably intertwined with a state proceeding.

(Choice C) The woman's claim would require the court to determine whether her investment in the cable service is a property interest protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause. But the fact that a claim raises an important constitutional question does not make it an actual case or controversy subject to judicial review.

Educational objective: When the plaintiff's harm is resolved, his/her claim becomes moot and must be dismissed unless (1) the harm is capable of repetition yet evading review or (2) the defendant voluntarily stops the challenged action but can resume it at any time.



选项正确率统计：A选项 8%，B选项 4%，C选项 5%，D选项 81%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

联邦法院有权裁决实际的案件和争议——即可通过司法解决的争端。但一旦原告的损害得到解决，其诉求就变得已失时效，应予以驳回，除非：

该损害可重复发生但规避审查，因为有合理的可能性，同样的损害将 (1) 再次影响原告，并且 (2) 持续时间不足以完成整个诉讼过程（例如，怀孕）或者被告自愿停止了被质疑的行为，但可以随时恢复。

在本案中，该女子在联邦法院提起诉讼，要求法官恢复对该男子谋杀案审判的电视直播。但在法院能够审理其诉求之前，这场争议已不复存在，因为该男子已被定罪和判刑。而且由于该男子的审判中没有明显错误，不足以支持重审，因此该争议不大可能重新出现。因此，该争议已失时效，联邦法院应批准法官的驳回动议。

(选项A) 该男子在上诉中成功的可能性极小。但即使他上诉成功并获得重审，电视摄像机是否会再次被禁止进入法庭也纯属猜测。因此，该女子的诉讼已失时效，应当被驳回，而不是推迟处理。

(选项B) 联邦法院在裁定诸如已失时效等程序性问题时，总是适用联邦法律——即便当联邦案件与州程序密不可分地交织在一起时也是如此。

(选项C) 该女子的诉求将要求法院确定她对有线电视服务的投资是否是受《Fourteenth Amendment》正当法律程序条款保护的一项财产权。但是，一项诉求提出了重要的宪法问题这一事实，并不会使其成为一个受司法审查的实际案件或争议。

教学目标：当原告的损害得到解决后，其诉求即已失时效，必须予以驳回，除非 (1) 该损害可重复发生但规避审查，或 (2) 被告自愿停止了被质疑的行为但可以随时恢复。

References

  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).
  • Turner v. Rogers, 564 U.S. 431, 439 - 40 (2011) (explaining the mootness doctrine and its exceptions).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 575 (2019) (defining mootness and its exceptions).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review
正确答案：D

批准该动议，因为该女子与法官之间的争议标的已不复存在，并且不大可能重新出现。

核心考点：Mootness (已失时效)

根据美国宪法第三条 (Article III)，联邦法院的管辖权仅限于"Cases and Controversies"（实际案件与争议）。

这意味着在诉讼的每一个阶段（包括审判和上诉），原告都必须拥有实际的、持续的利益争议。如果导致诉讼的事件已经结束或解决，法院无法再提供有效的救济，该案件即变为 Moot（已失时效），法院必须将其驳回。

本案逻辑推演
原告的诉求：该女子起诉的唯一目的是为了观看特定男子的审判直播。
现状变化：在案件审理前，该男子的审判已经结束（定罪并判刑）。
结果：法院现在即使发布禁令（Injunction）要求恢复直播，也无法执行，因为审判已经不存在了。争议标的消失。
例外情况排除：虽然存在“可重复发生但规避审查”的例外，但题目明确指出审判过程“没有明显错误”，这意味着重审（Retrial）的可能性极低，纯属猜测。因此，该例外不适用。
选项辨析
D (正确) Mootness Doctrine：争议已结束且无复发迹象，联邦法院无管辖权，必须驳回 (Dismiss)。
A (错误) Speculation (猜测)：法院不会基于“该男子可能会上诉成功”这种纯粹的猜测来维持案件。除非有合理的预期表明争议会重演，否则案件就是 Moot。
B (错误) Federal Law Governs：这是一个关于联邦法院管辖权 (Article III) 的问题。联邦法院在决定是否具有管辖权（如 Mootness）时，适用联邦法，而不是州法。
C (错误) Constitutional Importance：即使案件涉及重要的宪法问题（如第十四修正案财产权），如果它不再是一个“活的”争议 (Live Controversy)，法院也不能仅仅为了通过判决来确立法律原则而审理它。联邦法院不提供咨询意见 (Advisory Opinions)。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

当你在题目中看到“审判结束”、“法律被废除”或“活动已停止”时，立即联想 Mootness。

一定要检查是否有例外情况："Capable of repetition, yet evading review"（可重复发生但规避审查）。通常适用于：

  • 怀孕/堕胎案件 (Roe v. Wade)
  • 选举相关案件

如果题目像本题一样暗示“不太可能再次发生”（例如：没有明显错误导致重审），则必须驳回起诉。

questions.question:
The House of Representatives created an investigatory committee to look into the judicial administrative processes of federal judges. In particular, the committee was tasked with investigating the issuance of court orders, the management of trial schedules, and the drafting of basic court documents by judicial assistants. The goal of the committee was to ensure that the administrative processes were carried out efficiently, accurately, and pursuant to federal legislation regarding the judicial administrative process.
After much investigation, the committee concluded that a federal district court judge was negligently mismanaging his trial schedule, causing undue delays in his case log. Based upon its findings, the committee made a recommendation to the House of Representatives to remove the federal judge.
Can the House of Representatives remove the federal judge based on the committee's recommendation?

choices.a: No, because the House of Representatives cannot investigate a federal judge's administrative processes.
choices.b: No, because the federal judge can be removed only by impeachment.
choices.c: Yes, because the House of Representatives can remove federal judges with or without cause.
choices.d: Yes, because the federal judge mismanaged his trial schedule.

questions.question:
A consumer sued a business in state court for allegedly violating a state consumer-protection law. The law contains an ambiguous provision regarding the requirements for consumers to bring deceptive-practice claims against businesses in the state. This provision in the state law is identical to one in a federal consumer-protection act and relies in part on definitions contained in the federal act. In its defense, the business claimed that, based on the ambiguous provision, it could not be sued under the state law. When the case reached the state's highest court, that court sided with the business, but it was unclear whether the court relied on the interpretation of definitions contained in the federal act. The consumer petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court for review of the state court's decision.
Is it constitutional for the Supreme Court to review the state court's decision?

choices.a: No, because the consumer's action against the business involved a state, not federal, cause of action.
choices.b: No, because the state court's decision could rest on adequate and independent state grounds.
choices.c: Yes, because the Supreme Court may conclude that the state court decision relied upon the determination of a federal issue.
choices.d: Yes, because the Supreme Court may review any final judgment rendered by the highest court of a state.

questions.question:
A woman owns a luxury high-rise building in a large metropolitan area. The woman wanted to construct a helicopter pad on the roof of the building so that building residents could use a helicopter commuting service. A city inspector told the woman that she needed to apply for a permit to construct the helicopter pad, but he warned that the city would likely deny her application due to an existing zoning law. The woman promptly filed suit in federal court, seeking a declaratory judgment that the city's zoning law violates a federal law that prohibits state and local governments from restricting the provision of interstate transportation services to the public.
Which of the following is the city's best constitutional defense against this suit?

choices.a: Congress cannot regulate intrastate activity.
choices.b: The federal court should abstain from interfering with a city's regulatory scheme.
choices.c: The suit is barred by the Eleventh Amendment.
choices.d: The woman lacks standing to challenge the zoning law.

questions.question:
A political candidate wanted to run for office in an upcoming election and future elections. The candidate sought to be included on the state's ballot for the upcoming election, but she was unable to meet the requirements for certification.
The candidate filed suit in federal court against the proper representative of the state's electoral board, arguing that the state's requirements for ballot access are unduly burdensome and discriminatory. The district court ruled in favor of the electoral board, and the candidate timely filed an appeal. The election ended before the appellate court could hear the case. The state electoral board has moved to dismiss the candidate's appeal as moot.
How should the court rule on the state electoral board's motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the candidate's right to ballot access has been violated.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the challenged restrictions to ballot access will impact future elections.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because a live controversy no longer exists.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because any future injury to the candidate has become too speculative.

questions.question:
A trade association in State A was formed for the purpose of protecting the state's lucrative cattle industry. The association's members, who are cattle breeders and dealers, use a grading system to grade the quality of cattle bred in the state. The grades assigned by the association are nationally recognized and prominently displayed on cattle to promote the state's cattle industry.
The commissioner of the agency that regulates cattle in State B has adopted a regulation that requires cattle sold in the state to display a grade approved by the federal government or no grade at all. The sales in State B of several members of the trade association have declined as a result of complying with this regulation. As a result, the association has filed suit against the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the regulation on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
May the court determine the merits of this suit?

choices.a: No, because the association itself has suffered no injury.
choices.b: No, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against state officials in federal court.
choices.c: Yes, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over federal-law claims.
choices.d: Yes, because the association has standing to sue on behalf of its members.

questions.question:
Congress provides funds to states that can be used to reimburse medical providers for procedures they perform for low-income individuals. A state that participates in this federal program enacted a statute that prohibits reimbursing providers for the cost of performing vasectomies for men.
A doctor who routinely performs vasectomies for low-income men has submitted numerous requests for reimbursement pursuant to the program. However, the commissioner of the state agency administering the program has repeatedly denied the doctor's requests pursuant to the state statute.
The doctor sued the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the statute on the ground that it violates men's right to privacy.
Assuming that this federal district court has previously held that men have a privacy right to obtain vasectomies, how should the district court proceed with the doctor's suit?

choices.a: Determine the merits of the suit, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over federal-law claims.
choices.b: Determine the merits of the suit, because the doctor has standing.
choices.c: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and dismiss it, because the Eleventh Amendment bars this type of action in federal court.
choices.d: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and stay the suit until a man seeking a vasectomy joins the suit.

questions.question:
An individual was physically removed from the premises of a privately owned shopping mall for passing out flyers in support of a candidate for mayor of the city in which the mall was located. The individual challenged this action in state court, contending that her removal violated the free speech provisions in both the U.S. and state constitutions. The trial court ruled in the individual's favor, and the mall properly appealed. The state supreme court concluded: "We hold that the state constitution, which protects free speech on privately owned property in certain situations, was clearly violated by the mall's conduct." The court declined to address the issue of whether that conduct violated the federal Constitution.
The United States Supreme Court granted a writ of certiorari to review this decision of the state supreme court.
How should the United States Supreme Court rule?

choices.a: Affirm the state supreme court's decision.
choices.b: Dismiss the writ as improvidently granted.
choices.c: Remand the case to the state supreme court.
choices.d: Reverse the state supreme court's decision.

questions.question:
A federal statute, applicable to all public and private employers, makes discrimination against persons with a certain disability in the hiring or firing of employees illegal. It also provides for a civil action for damages against the offending employer. The statute contains a clear statement of Congressional intent to abrogate state immunity pursuant to its powers under the Fourteenth Amendment.
An employee sued her employer in federal court for violation of this statute and sought relief in the form of retroactive money damages. The employer, a state agency, moved to dismiss the action as constitutionally prohibited. The employee conceded that the state agency's acts, like most historical acts of discrimination against individuals with this particular disability, were rationally related to a legitimate government purpose.
Should the court dismiss the action on constitutional grounds?

choices.a: No, because Congress enacted the statute pursuant to its constitutional power under the Enabling Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.b: No, because Congress was acting pursuant to its power under the Commerce Clause.
choices.c: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prevents the recovery of retroactive money damages by citizens against a state agency.
choices.d: Yes, because the state agency's actions did not violate the Equal Protection Clause.

questions.question:
A federal statute enacted pursuant to the power of Congress to enforce the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits any state from requiring any of its employees to retire from state employment solely because of their age. The statute expressly authorizes employees required by a state to retire from state employment solely because of their age to sue the state government in federal district court for any damages resulting from that state action.
On the basis of this federal statute, a retiree sues State X in federal district court. State X moves to dismiss the suit on the ground that Congress lacks authority to authorize such suits against a state.
Which of the following is the strongest argument that the retiree can offer in opposition to the state's motion to dismiss this suit?

choices.a: When Congress exercises power vested in it by any provision of the Constitution, Congress has unlimited authority to authorize private actions for damages against a state.
choices.b: When Congress exercises power vested in it by the Fourteenth Amendment, Congress may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.
choices.c: While the Eleventh Amendment applies to suits in federal court by citizens of one state against another state, it does not apply to such suits by citizens against their own states.
choices.d: While the Eleventh Amendment restrains the federal judiciary, that amendment does not limit the power of Congress to modify the sovereign immunity of the states.

一项根据国会执行 Fourteenth Amendment 的权力而制定的联邦法规，禁止任何州仅因年龄原因要求其任何雇员从州政府部门退休。该法规明确授权因年龄原因被州政府要求退休的雇员，可就该州行为造成的任何损害，在联邦地区法院向州政府提起诉讼。

基于此联邦法规，一名退休人员在联邦地区法院起诉 X 州。X 州以国会无权授权此类针对州的诉讼为由，请求驳回该诉讼。

以下哪项是该退休人员可以提出的、用以反对该州驳回此诉讼动议的最有力论点？
options:
A. When Congress exercises power vested in it by any provision of the Constitution, Congress has unlimited authority to authorize private actions for damages against a state.
当国会行使宪法任何条款授予它的权力时，国会拥有无限的权力来授权针对州的私人损害赔偿诉讼。

B. When Congress exercises power vested in it by the Fourteenth Amendment, Congress may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.
当国会行使其由 Fourteenth Amendment 授予的权力时，国会可以制定适当的补救性法律，明确规定州政府须在联邦法院接受私人损害赔偿诉讼。

C. While the Eleventh Amendment applies to suits in federal court by citizens of one state against another state, it does not apply to such suits by citizens against their own states.
虽然 Eleventh Amendment 适用于一个州的公民在联邦法院对另一个州提起的诉讼，但它不适用于公民对本州提起的此类诉讼。

D. While the Eleventh Amendment restrains the federal judiciary, that amendment does not limit the power of Congress to modify the sovereign immunity of the states.
虽然 Eleventh Amendment 限制了联邦司法系统，但该修正案并不限制国会修改各州主权豁免的权力。

(11A does not apply)
  • State consents to suit
  • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
  • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief
  • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
  • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
The Eleventh Amendment generally forbids the federal courts from hearing private suits for damages against the states. Congress cannot override this ban, even to exercise one of its constitutionally enumerated powers (Choices A & D). But there is a narrow exception to this rule when Congress is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments (eg, Fourteenth Amendment - as seen here). In that case, it may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment applies to all private suits for damages against the states - including suits by citizens against their own state. But it does not bar Congress from authorizing such suits as a means of enforcing the Civil War Amendments.

Educational objective: The Eleventh Amendment generally forbids the federal courts from hearing private suits for damages against the states. But Congress can authorize such suits when it is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments (ie, Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments).

豁免权

  • 豁免权被 13th, 14th, 或 15th Amendment 废除

  • 州官员因将来的（而非追溯性的）损害赔偿被诉，且赔偿金由州财政支付

Eleventh Amendment 通常禁止联邦法院审理针对州的私人损害赔偿诉讼。国会不能 推翻此项禁令，即使是为了行使其宪法列举的一项权力 （选项 A 和 D）。但当国会明确地为了执行《内战修正案》（Civil War Amendments）（例如，本案中的 Fourteenth Amendment）而采取行动时，此规则有一个狭窄的例外。在这种情况下，国会可以制定适当的补救性法律，明确规定州政府须在联邦法院接受私人损害赔偿诉讼。

（选项 C） Eleventh Amendment 适用于针对州的所有私人损害赔偿诉讼——包括公民对本州提起的诉讼。但它并不阻止国会为执行《内战修正案》而授权此类诉讼。

教学目标： Eleventh Amendment 通常禁止联邦法院审理针对州的私人损害赔偿诉讼。但当国会明确为了执行《内战修正案》（即 Thirteenth、Fourteenth 和 Fifteenth Amendments）而采取行动时，国会可以授权此类诉讼。

References

United States v. Georgia, 546 U.S. 151, 158 - 59 (2006) (explaining that the Fourteenth Amendment allows Congress to abrogate state sovereign immunity by authorizing private suits for damages against the states).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Sovereign Immunity
正确答案：选项 B

这是最强有力的论点：当国会行使 Fourteenth Amendment（第十四修正案）授予的权力时，可以明确废除各州的主权豁免权。

核心法律规则解析

1. 第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 的一般原则

通常情况下，Eleventh Amendment 禁止联邦法院审理私人针对“州”（State）的损害赔偿诉讼。这就是所谓的州主权豁免 (State Sovereign Immunity)。

2. 国会的废除权 (Abrogation)

国会想要废除各州的这种豁免权，必须满足两个条件：

  • 明确表达 (Unequivocally express)： 国会必须在立法中明确表示要允许针对州的诉讼。
  • 合法的权力来源 (Valid source of power)： 这是本题的关键。

3. 权力来源的区别 (The Critical Distinction)

这是 MBE 宪法部分的高频考点，请务必区分：

  • ❌ Article I Powers (如 Commerce Clause): 国会不能利用第一条的权力（如商务条款）来废除第十一修正案的豁免权。
    Seminole Tribe v. Florida (1996)
  • ✅ 14th Amendment, Section 5: 国会可以利用第十四修正案第 5 款（执行条款）来废除豁免权。因为第十四修正案是在第十一修正案之后通过的，它从根本上改变了联邦与州权力的平衡。
    Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer (1976)
本题逻辑分析

题目中明确指出：

  1. 该法规是根据国会执行 Fourteenth Amendment 的权力制定的。
  2. 该法规明确授权 (expressly authorizes) 雇员起诉州政府。

因此，退休人员最有力的反驳就是指出国会是在行使第十四修正案的权力，这是废除州主权豁免的合法途径。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误： 声称国会行使“任何”宪法权力都能废除豁免权是错误的。如前所述，行使 Article I (如商务条款) 的权力是无效的。
选项 C 错误： 这是一个常见的陷阱。虽然第十一修正案的文本只提到了“他州公民”，但最高法院在 Hans v. Louisiana (1890) 中确立，主权豁免原则同样禁止本州公民在联邦法院起诉自己的州。
选项 D 错误： 这过于宽泛。第十一修正案确实限制了国会修改主权豁免的权力（限制了国会使用 Article I powers），除非国会使用的是第十四修正案的权力。
MBE 备考建议：看到 "State Sovereign Immunity" 时，立即检查国会的权力来源是 Article I (无效) 还是 14th Amendment (有效)。

Eleventh Amendment
(state immunity from suit in federal court)


ImmunityNo immunity
Suit brought by private party or foreign government

Suit against state official violating state law

Exceptions:
  • State consents to suit
  • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment

  • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury

The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state for money damages or equitable relief in federal court. Congress can abrogate (ie, repeal) this immunity if it is clearly acting to enforce a Civil War Amendment - ie, the Thirteenth, Fourteenth , or Fifteenth Amendment (not seen here). Congress may then enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

However, Congress cannot abrogate a state's Eleventh Amendment immunity through its other powers.† This includes its Article I power to enact laws protecting copyrighted materials (Choice A). This also includes its power under Articles I and III to regulate the jurisdiction of the federal courts (Choice B). Therefore, the court will likely grant the state's motion to dismiss the photographer's suit pursuant to the Eleventh Amendment.

†The lone exception to this rule is that Congress may subject nonconsenting states to bankruptcy proceedings through the Article I bankruptcy clause. The Supreme Court has justified this exception based on the bankruptcy clause's unique history and exceptionalism.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment prohibits the federal government from compelling states to enact state laws or enforce federal laws. However, states can be subjected to suits for damages in federal court if Congress validly abrogates state immunity.

Educational objective: The Eleventh Amendment generally grants states immunity from suits for damages. Congress can abrogate this immunity when it clearly acts to enforce a Civil War Amendment but cannot do so through its other powers - eg, its powers to protect copyrights and regulate federal court jurisdiction.
